findings.rationale: CA's uploaded updates are about 3.7x the median norm (size-adjusted z=+7.1) in every round from round 1, and the cosine to the median update jumps erratically between strongly negative (-0.35 in round 4), near zero, and near 1 (round 7). That is the signature of large random noise added to uploads rather than a consistent sign flip or scaling. CA's local AUC (0.83) and CITL (0.005) are normal, so accuracy barely moves. Global attribution churn is also high (rank correlation with the previous round near zero or negative in several rounds), consistent with noisy uploads contaminating the global explanations.

IA's updates are about 3.2x the median norm (size-adjusted z=+6.4) in every round from round 1, with cosine to the median swinging from -0.29 (round 12) to 1.0 (round 5) and mostly near zero in later rounds. This is the pattern of random noise in uploads. IA's local AUC (0.845) and CITL (0.009) are normal, so accuracy is not affected.

SC's updates are about 3.2x the median norm (size-adjusted z=+6.5) in every round from round 1, with cosine to the median fluctuating between about -0.25 and +0.70 across rounds. That is consistent with large random noise in uploads. SC's local AUC (0.80) and CITL (-0.019) are within the federation range, so accuracy barely moves.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the update, performance, drift, feature and subgroup tools (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed suspects with narrower per-client update queries and attribution churn. Three clients (CA, IA, SC) have update norms about 3x the median in every round from round 1, with erratic cosine to the median and normal local accuracy. That matches explanation_instability (random noise in uploads), not poisoning, since the cosine does not hold a consistent sign. Global attribution churn is high, which fits. I report these three with confidence 0.7. Other leads were not reported as faults: CT's AgeGroup-1 subgroup outlier (z_noise 5.3, but the direction is over- not under-prediction and the client's overall performance is normal), VI's Sex-0 FNR and feature tail outliers, GU's small-sample outliers, and several single small-client feature outliers. None reached the consistent evidence needed. Budget is fully spent (20.0 used).
